sourceNote.title: Checkout address form
sourceNote.html:
Checkout shipping address

Testing the new shipping address step in a demo web shop (staging build 2.4.0).

  • Fields: full name, street and number, postcode, city, country (dropdown, NL/BE/DE).

  • Postcode format depends on country: NL is 4 digits + 2 letters (1234 AB, space optional), BE and DE are 4 and 5 digits.

  • Name max 60 characters; street max 100.

  • Continue button is disabled until all required fields are filled. Errors show inline under the field after leaving it.

  • Changing country after typing a postcode re-validates the postcode.

  • Observed: pasting a postcode with a trailing space for NL showed an error, typing the same value did not.

  • Observed: the address is kept when going back from payment to shipping.

bodyHtml:
Chosen technique: Equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis, supplemented by state-transition coverage for country changes, validation timing, and navigation. Recorded observations are preserved as regression evidence.

Scenario: Required address fields and validation timing

Test case: Continue availability as required fields are completed

Purpose: Verify the required-field gate.

Preconditions: Checkout shipping address is open in staging build 2.4.0.

Test data: Full name: Test Shopper; street and number: Teststraat 1; postcode: 1234 AB; city: Teststad; country: NL.

  • Leave the address fields empty and inspect Continue.

  • Populate the fields progressively, inspecting Continue while each required field remains unfilled.

  • Complete all required fields with the test data and inspect Continue.

Expected result: Continue is disabled while any required field is unfilled. With all required fields filled using valid data, Continue is available.

Coverage notes: The note does not individually identify which fields are required; confirm the required-field set from the form before execution.

Test case: Invalid postcode error appears after leaving the field

Purpose: Verify inline error timing and placement.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open with NL selected and no postcode error displayed.

Test data: Invalid NL postcode: 123.

  • Enter 123 in the postcode field while keeping focus in that field.

  • Move focus to the city field.

  • Inspect the postcode field and the area beneath it.

Expected result: The postcode error appears inline under the field after focus leaves it.

Coverage notes: Exact error wording is not specified.

Scenario: Country-specific postcode formats

Test case: NL postcode accepts optional internal space and rejects invalid structure

Purpose: Verify the NL postcode format.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open with NL selected.

Test data: Valid: 1234 AB, 1234AB. Invalid: 123 AB, 12345 AB, 1234 A, 1234 ABC, 1234 12.

  • Enter each valid value separately and leave the postcode field.

  • Replace the postcode with each invalid value separately and leave the field.

Expected result: Both valid values pass postcode validation. Each invalid value shows an inline postcode error after leaving the field.

Coverage notes: Covers optional spacing, digit-count boundaries, letter-count boundaries, and a non-letter suffix. Letter-case behavior is unspecified.

Test case: BE postcode requires four digits

Purpose: Verify BE postcode length and character restrictions.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open with BE selected.

Test data: Valid: 1234. Invalid: 123, 12345, 123A.

  • Enter each test value separately and leave the postcode field.

  • Inspect validation after each value.

Expected result: 1234 passes postcode validation. Three digits, five digits, and a value containing a letter show inline postcode errors.

Coverage notes: Covers the specified four-digit format and adjacent length boundaries; geographic postcode validity is not specified.

Test case: DE postcode requires five digits

Purpose: Verify DE postcode length and character restrictions.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open with DE selected.

Test data: Valid: 12345. Invalid: 1234, 123456, 1234A.

  • Enter each test value separately and leave the postcode field.

  • Inspect validation after each value.

Expected result: 12345 passes postcode validation. Four digits, six digits, and a value containing a letter show inline postcode errors.

Coverage notes: Covers the specified five-digit format and adjacent length boundaries; geographic postcode validity is not specified.

Test case: Country changes revalidate an existing postcode

Purpose: Verify postcode validation follows the selected country.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open.

Test data: Postcodes: 1234, 12345. Countries: NL, BE, DE.

  • Inspect the country dropdown for NL, BE, and DE.

  • Select BE, enter 1234, and leave the postcode field.

  • Change the country to DE without editing the postcode and inspect validation.

  • Replace the postcode with 12345 and leave the field.

  • Change the country to NL without editing the postcode and inspect validation.

  • Change the country back to DE and inspect validation.

Expected result: The dropdown offers NL, BE, and DE. The value 1234 passes for BE and fails after switching to DE. The value 12345 passes for DE, fails after switching to NL, and passes again after switching back to DE. Country changes trigger revalidation without postcode edits.

Coverage notes: Covers valid-to-invalid and invalid-to-valid transitions across all three countries.

Scenario: Address text length limits

Test case: Full name at and above the 60-character limit

Purpose: Verify the full-name maximum length.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open.

Test data: Full-name strings of 59, 60, and 61 characters, constructed from repeated A characters.

  • Enter each test string separately in the full-name field and leave the field.

  • Inspect the retained value and any inline validation.

Expected result: Values of 59 and 60 characters do not fail length validation. A 61-character name cannot be accepted as a valid value.

Coverage notes: Covers immediately below, at, and above the maximum. The note does not specify whether excess characters are blocked or an inline error is shown.

Test case: Street and number at and above the 100-character limit

Purpose: Verify the street-field maximum length.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open.

Test data: Strings of 99, 100, and 101 characters: respectively 97, 98, and 99 repeated A characters followed by “ 1”.

  • Enter each test string separately in the street and number field and leave the field.

  • Inspect the retained value and any inline validation.

Expected result: Values of 99 and 100 characters do not fail length validation. A 101-character street value cannot be accepted as valid.

Coverage notes: Covers immediately below, at, and above the maximum. The note does not specify how excess characters are handled.

Scenario: Recorded postcode entry and navigation behavior

Test case: Compare pasted and typed NL postcodes with a trailing space

Purpose: Recheck the recorded difference between paste and typing.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open with NL selected. Start each entry method with an empty postcode field.

Test data: 1234 AB followed by one trailing space, entered identically through paste and typing.

  • Paste the test value into the postcode field, leave the field, and record validation.

  • Clear the field, type the identical value including its trailing space, leave the field, and record validation.

  • Compare the outcomes for both entry methods.

Expected result: The recorded observation was an error for a pasted NL postcode with a trailing space and no error when the same value was typed. Record whether that difference remains reproducible.

Coverage notes: Preserves the note’s observation. The exact original postcode and intended trailing-space handling are unspecified, so this is a characterization case rather than a defined acceptance rule.

Test case: Shipping address persists when returning from payment

Purpose: Verify the recorded address retention behavior.

Preconditions: Shipping address is open and the checkout can proceed to payment.

Test data: Full name: Test Shopper; street and number: Teststraat 1; postcode: 1234 AB; city: Teststad; country: NL.

  • Populate the shipping address with the test data.

  • Select Continue to reach payment.

  • Go back from payment to shipping.

  • Compare all address field values with the entered data.

Expected result: Full name, street and number, postcode, city, and country remain populated with the entered address.

Coverage notes: Preserves the observed retention when returning from payment. Refresh, session expiry, and browser restart behavior are outside the supplied note.
